notes: EBIT definition: JNJ does not present a labeled 'Operating income' / 'EBIT' line in the extracted statement table; EBIT here is modeled as Gross profit - Selling, marketing & administrative - R&D - In-process R&D impairments - Restructuring (all from consolidated statements of earnings). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000200406/000020040626000016/jnj-20251228.htm))

Working capital (NWC) definition for this package: (Total current assets - Cash & cash equivalents - Marketable securities) - (Total current liabilities - Loans and notes payable). NWC can be negative (as observed in historical data). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000200406/000020040626000016/jnj-20251228.htm))

Tax rate: base-case uses a normalized effective tax rate assumption of 0.17, anchored to reported effective tax rates for continuing operations (17.7% in 2025; 15.7% in 2024). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000200406/000020040626000016/jnj-20251228.htm))

Cash/debt/investments: cash = cash & cash equivalents; investments = marketable securities (short-term). Debt = Loans and notes payable + Long-term debt. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000200406/000020040626000016/jnj-20251228.htm))

NOL fields: JNJ discloses 'Net operating loss & tax credit carryforwards' within deferred tax disclosures, but not a standalone NOL principal balance and NOL utilization percent suitable for direct DCF tax-shield modeling in this pass; therefore nol_balance and nol_utilization_pct are set to null.

WACC, terminal growth, and scenario deltas are modeling assumptions (not directly sourced from filings/consensus); adjust if your pipeline uses a different capital structure or discount-rate framework.
Stock price: current_price set to $235.37 from the latest available market data timestamp provided by the pricing lookup tool (trade time 2026-03-20 UTC).

catalysts: 2026 execution vs. guidance (sales growth and adjusted EPS trajectory) provides near-term directional confirmation for the DCF path. ([investor.jnj.com](https://investor.jnj.com/investor-news/news-details/2026/Johnson--Johnson-reports-Q4-and-Full-Year-2025-results/default.aspx))

Major portfolio launches/label expansions in Innovative Medicine could lift growth above the base-case trajectory. ([investor.jnj.com](https://investor.jnj.com/investor-news/news-details/2026/Johnson--Johnson-reports-Q4-and-Full-Year-2025-results/default.aspx))

MedTech innovation/adoption cycles could continue to support mid-single-digit revenue growth even as legacy products mature. ([s203.q4cdn.com](https://s203.q4cdn.com/636242992/files/doc_news/Johnson--Johnson-reports-Q4-and-Full-Year-2025-results-2026.pdf))
company_overview: Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) operates in two reporting segments: Innovative Medicine and MedTech. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000200406/000020040626000016/jnj-20251228.htm))

Innovative Medicine is focused across oncology, immunology, neuroscience, pulmonary hypertension, infectious diseases, and cardiovascular/metabolism therapeutic areas. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000200406/000020040626000016/jnj-20251228.htm))

MedTech spans cardiovascular and other surgical/vision-adjacent medical technologies, supporting recurring demand in elective and chronic care cycles. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000200406/000020040626000016/jnj-20251228.htm))
current_context: On 2026-01-21, JNJ reported FY2025 sales of $94.193B (+6.0% reported) and guided FY2026 to midpoint reported sales of $100.5B (+6.7%) and adjusted EPS of $11.53 (+6.9%). ([investor.jnj.com](https://investor.jnj.com/investor-news/news-details/2026/Johnson--Johnson-reports-Q4-and-Full-Year-2025-results/default.aspx))

Management highlighted FY2025 as an acceleration year, with FY2025 free cash flow estimated at ~$19.7B. ([investor.jnj.com](https://investor.jnj.com/investor-news/news-details/2026/Johnson--Johnson-reports-Q4-and-Full-Year-2025-results/default.aspx))
investment_highlights: Base-case revenue growth decelerates from the FY2026 guided run-rate toward a mid/late-cycle steady state consistent with the terminal growth assumption (2%). ([investor.jnj.com](https://investor.jnj.com/investor-news/news-details/2026/Johnson--Johnson-reports-Q4-and-Full-Year-2025-results/default.aspx))

EBIT margin is modeled to remain broadly stable with modest improvement versus FY2024, reflecting operating leverage and disciplined reinvestment (capex ~5% of sales). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000200406/000020040626000016/jnj-20251228.htm))

Historically, JNJ exhibits negative net working capital (rebates/payables dynamics), which is carried forward in the model as a working-capital tailwind. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000200406/000020040626000016/jnj-20251228.htm))

Tax rate is anchored to recent effective tax levels from continuing operations rather than a static statutory rate. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000200406/000020040626000016/jnj-20251228.htm))
key_risks: Patent expiry, biosimilar competition, and reimbursement pressure could reduce organic growth and/or pressure EBIT margin vs. assumptions. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000200406/000020040626000016/jnj-20251228.htm))
Working-capital dynamics (rebates/collections/payables) may normalize, reducing the modeled tailwind from negative NWC.

Regulatory, manufacturing, and litigation risks can create discrete charges that affect profitability and cash flow timing. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000200406/000020040626000016/jnj-20251228.htm))

presentation.subtitle: JNJ: FY2025 Base-Case DCF Input Package (2026–2030)
valuation_summary: DCF base-case is anchored on FY2025 actuals (revenue, operating cash-flow components, and balance-sheet working capital inputs) from JNJ’s FY2025 Form 10-K. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000200406/000020040626000016/jnj-20251228.htm))

Reinvestment intensity is modeled via capex as a percent of sales and depreciation as a percent of sales, both tied to recent historical averages. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000200406/000020040626000016/jnj-20251228.htm))
Terminal value uses a Gordon growth approach (terminal method = gordon_growth) with terminal growth set to 2.0% to reflect long-run macro conditions.
